chapters.title: The Sanctity of the Righteous of the Old Law, and of Joseph and of Mary herself, consisted in Fidelity to the Order of God
The Duties of each Moment are the Shadows which veil the Divine Action
How much Easier Sanctity becomes when studied from this Point of View
Perfection does not consist in knowing the Order of God, but in submitting to it
Reading and other Exercises only sanctify us in so far as they are the Channels of the Divine Action
The Mind and other Human Means are Useful only in as far as they are the Instruments of the Divine Action
There is no Enduring Peace but in Submission to the Divine Action
The Perfection of Souls and the Excellence of Different States are in Proportion to their Conformity to the Order of God
All the Riches of Grace are the Fruit of Purity of Heart and Perfect Self-abandonment
The Divine Action is everywhere and always Present, though only Visible to the Eye of Faith
The Divine Action is all the more Visible to the Eye of Faith when hidden under Appearances most Repugnant to the Senses
The Divine Action offers us at each Moment Infinite Blessings, which we receive in proportion to our Faith and Love
God reveals Himself to us as Mysteriously, as Adorably, and with as much Reality in the most Ordinary Events as in the great Events of History and the Holy Scriptures
The Divine Action continues in our Hearts the Revelation begun in Holy Scripture; but the Characters in which it is written will be Visible only at the Last Day
Divine Love is communicated to us through the Veil of Creatures, as Jesus communicates Himself to us through the Veil of the Eucharistic Species
The Divine Action, the Will of God, is as unworthily treated and disregarded in its Daily Manifestation by many Christians as was Jesus in the Flesh by the Jews
The Revelation of the Present Moment is the more Profitable that it is addressed Directly to us
The Revelation of the Present Moment is an Inexhaustible Source of Sanctity
The Present Moment is the Manifestation of the Name of God and the Coming of His Kingdom
The Divine Will imparts the Highest Sanctity to Souls; they have but to abandon Themselves to its Divine Action
The Divine Action alone can sanctify us, for it forms us after the Divine Model of our Perfection
God Himself guides Souls who wholly abandon themselves to Him
The more God seems to withdraw Light from the Soul abandoned to His Direction, the more Safely He guides Her
The Afflictions with which God visits the Soul are but Loving Artifices at which she will One Day rejoice
The more God seems to take from a Soul wholly abandoned to Him, the more Generous He is to her
The less Capable the Faithful Soul is of defending Herself, the more Powerfully does God defend Her
The Soul abandoned to the Will of God, so far from resisting her Enemies, finds in them Useful Auxiliaries
The Soul who abandons Herself to God has no Need to justify Herself by Words or Actions: the Divine Action justifies Her
God gives Life to the Soul abandoned to Him by Means which apparently lead only to Death
Love holds the Place of All Things to Souls who walk in the Way of Abandonment
The Faithful Soul finds in Submission to the Will of God more Force and Strength than the Proudest of those who resist Him
The Soul abandoned to God learns to recognize His Will even in the Proud who resist Him. All Creatures, whether Good or Evil, reveal Him to her
God assures to Faithful Souls a Glorious Victory over the Powers of Earth and Hell
